notes: Balancing authority is NV Energy (SGIP grid-region listing shows Truckee Donner PUD = SGIP_NVENERGY), not CAISO/BANC, so WECC-nonRTO. Optional residential TOU rate (peak 4-9pm) and Customer Generator TOU rate. Commercial: only new EV-charging commercial rate (Small/Medium/Large EV Commercial) is TOU-designed; standard commercial rate is flat/demand-charge only and FAQ states general commercial TOU 'not yet' offered. No residential device-dispatch program found (rebates + BESS feasibility study only, no BYOD/thermostat/water-heater control). Business programs page says commercial programs 'being remodeled', no interruptible/curtailable rider found.

SGIP grid-region listing shows City of Banning = SGIP_CAISO_SCE, i.e. within SCE's CAISO DLAP -> CAISO. RS-1 residential tariff is flat energy charge only, no TOU/CPP/demand rate. MC-1 (Medium Commercial) and IS-1 (Industrial) tariffs are flat energy + plain (non-shifting) demand charge, not TOU-designed. IW-1 Interruptible Well Service rider explicitly interrupts during CAISO Flex Alerts -- counts as ci_dispatch. Residential rebates page (banningca.gov/122 and /300) is JS-rendered/unreadable directly; a search-cached list mentions a 'Thermostat Rebate' among efficiency rebates (refrigerator recycling, shade tree, weatherization) but no language indicating utility device control/DR enrollment, so res_dispatch left Unknown rather than guessed.

SGIP grid-region listing shows Merced Irrigation District (MeID) = SGIP_TID, i.e. within Turlock Irrigation District balancing authority territory, not a CAISO DLAP -> WECC-nonRTO. RES-2 residential rate is a flat two-tier inverted-block energy charge (no TOU/CPP). EGS-2 (small C&I <35kW) is flat customer+energy charge, no demand or TOU component; larger C&I schedules (ED-4/ED-3/ED-2/ED-1P/TR-1) are named by demand tier only (Small/Medium/Large Demand General Service), no TOU or RTP language on the electric-rates schedule list. Residential rebates page (for-my-home) lists only appliance, heating/cooling, and HVAC tune-up rebates -- no device-control/DR enrollment program. Business rebates page (for-my-business/business-rebates) is an efficiency-retrofit incentive program (kWh/kW-based rebates for equipment upgrades), not an interruptible/curtailable rider; full electric-rates schedule list has no interruptible/curtailable/DR schedule (unlike neighboring Banning IW-1).

SGIP grid-region listing shows Lassen Municipal Utility District = SGIP_CAISO_PGE (within PG&E's CAISO DLAP) -> CAISO. All rate schedules (Domestic/Residential 1010, General Service 1020, General Service Demand 1025, Industrial 1070, Reactive/Stand-by/Supplementary, Agricultural 1030) are flat per-kWh commodity charges (plus plain per-kW demand charge for Demand/Industrial/Reactive schedules), no TOU, CPP, or RTP design found; LMUD board discussed a residential TOU pilot at its Sept 23, 2025 meeting but no live TOU rate found on the rates page. Residential Smart Thermostat rebate is a $30 mail-in rebate for replacing an old mercury thermostat (via directefficiency.com/thermostatcare.org), not a utility-controlled/DR-enrolled smart-thermostat program. Business Rebates page lists only energy-efficiency programs (HVAC, lighting, clothes washer, kitchen equipment, custom efficiency projects), no interruptible/curtailable rider or aggregator-facing DR found; Reactive/Stand-by/Supplementary schedule (1080-1083) is for customers with their own generation (standby/backup), not a utility-dispatched curtailment program.
